small_guidance:
- Reduce redundant work: the kernel reads x twice (stats pass + normalize pass). Cache the ReLU'd values into the output buffer on the first pass, then re-read from out_ptr (or keep in registers for small S) to avoid recomputing maximum.
- Try BLOCK_S=4096 or 8192 with num_warps=8/16 and num_stages=2 — at S=34*34*34≈39304 per group-channel, fewer iterations of the outer s-loop reduces loop overhead. Also try parallelizing over (N, group, channel-chunk) with a second-stage reduction since C_PER_GROUP=16 is serialized today.
- The conv_transpose3d dominates runtime (~7ms baseline); group-norm fusion is already mostly there. Verify by profiling — if conv is >80% of time, tuning the norm kernel further yields <10% gain.
large_guidance:
- Replace nn.ConvTranspose3d with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile), computing the outer product of input × weight[ic, :, kd, kh, kw] and atomic-adding into the output grid at (n, oc, d+kd, h+kh, w+kw). With kernel_size=3, stride=1, padding=0, the output is 34³ — manageable for atomics. This is the high-headroom move since conv_transpose is ~70%+ of runtime.
- Alternatively, implement conv_transpose as a gather: each output element (n, oc, od, oh, ow) sums over (ic, kd, kh, kw) of input[n, ic, od-kd, oh-kh, ow-kw] * weight[ic, oc, kd, kh, kw], with bounds checks. This avoids atomics and tiles cleanly as a GEMM with K=IC*27.
- Fuse ReLU + GroupNorm stats accumulation into the conv epilogue: emit channels-last output and have each conv program contribute partial sum_x / sum_x2 to a per-(N, group) workspace via atomics, then a tiny second kernel finalizes mean/rstd and a third applies the affine. Or split into conv→relu+stats kernel and normalize kernel, eliminating the double-read of the conv output.
